newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends down on weak sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends down on weak sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down on Thursday on weak sentiment, after copper was unable to breach the $1,950 resistance level on the London Metal Exchange last night and ahead of a national holiday, traders said.
The most active January 1997 contract closed at 19,940 yuan ($2,401) per tonne, down 170 yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 20,110 and hit a low of 19,900.
October fell 160 to 20,300 yuan, November 110 to 20,130, December 130 to 20,020, February 180 to 19,920, March 150 to 19,980 and April 170 to 19,980.
Combined volume rose slightly to 32,780 tonnes from 32,740.
"Open interest has decreased every day because many investors did not want to hold positions during the holiday," a second trader said. "Copper will not move sharply in the next few days."
Traders said trading will be dull in the next few days.
Aluminium ended up in slow trading. October rose 20 to 13,900 yuan per tonne and November 70 to 13,870.
Combined volume fell to 220 tonnes from 430.
